correctness.rationale: Fixing the distinguished chord leaves \((N-1)!!\) equiprobable matchings. Counting \(h\) cross-cut pairs gives \(p_{n,k}(h)\), and direct factorial division gives the claimed ratio. Its varying factor has strictly positive derivative because \(N-2k-2>0\) for \(0\le k\le n-3\). Added support at \(h=k+2\) makes same-parity stochastic order strict; parity support at zero and the exact top-tail ratio \((N-2k)/(N-k)<1\) show adjacent incomparability for \(1\le k\le n-2\), while \(k=0\) is deterministic. Indicator linearity verifies the mean. The standalone verifier independently enumerates matchings through 14 endpoints and passes 128 rational assertions. Quantifiers hold for every \(n\ge3\); experiments are not substituted for infinite proof.

value.rationale: Degree of a uniformly sampled chord conditional on its geometric shorter-arc span is a natural local network statistic studied in primary literature. The theorem supplies sharp all-n finite-sample distributional control along parity classes and demonstrates that *every* adjacent positive length comparison is stochastically incomparable in spite of increasing mean; both features matter for predicting tails from span. The result is not just an expectation identity or an arbitrary small-parameter census.
